transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um, yeah—so, I guess the main thing is at work I keep leaving my station when I’m supposed to stay there. Like I’ll just pop up or walk off before I even really think about it, and then I’m already halfway across the floor. It happens in meetings too, like I’m supposed to sit and listen but I’m up grabbing something or moving around.

My supervisor’s been on me about it because it’s becoming a safety thing, especially on the floor. And I don’t know, I’m not trying to be difficult—I just kind of take off and then realize after. It’s been getting me in trouble, so that’s why I’m here.
Did you have this same habit of getting out of your seat or walking off impulsively when you were a child?

Yeah, definitely. Like even in elementary school, I was that kid who just could not stay in her seat. I’d be up wandering around the classroom, or I’d talk right over the teacher without meaning to. My mom used to get those little notes sent home, like “she needs to stay seated” or “she’s blurting out,” stuff like that.

I remember one time—well, not one time, a lot of times—I’d get up to sharpen a pencil or throw something away and then end up by somebody else’s desk talking, and the teacher would be like, “Sit down, please.” So yeah, it’s kind of always been a thing.
Have you ever had a stretch of time when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or unusually irritable compared with your normal self?

Um… I don’t think so? Like, I get irritated sometimes, but I feel like that’s pretty normal, like if work’s been a mess or somebody’s pushing my buttons. But unusually high or euphoric… I don’t know, not that I’ve really noticed.

When you say “stretch of time,” do you mean like days where I’m acting totally different? Because I can be in a really good mood if something good happens, like getting paid or making plans, but I wouldn’t say it’s, like, out of nowhere or anything.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when you want to?

Yeah… yeah, I do. Like at work, when I’m doing the inventory logs, I’ll start out really trying to pay attention, like I’m telling myself, “Okay, just get through this.” But after a few minutes the numbers start kind of blending together, and then I realize I’ve been looking at the same line and didn’t actually take it in.

Same with the CNC training pages. I’ll read a section and then I’m like, wait, what did that even say? So I have to keep going back over it. It’s frustrating because I do want to get it done, but my brain just kind of slips off it.
Do you often feel restless, like you have to keep moving even when you’re trying to sit still?

Yeah, all the time. Like if I’m standing by the machine and I’m supposed to just stay there and watch it, I start feeling this pressure building up in my body, like I need to move right now. I’ll shift around, stretch, pace a little if I can.

And sitting through training is bad too. I’ll be trying to listen, but my legs are going, or I’m thinking, “I need to get up and do something.” It’s not even always that I want to leave, it just feels like my body won’t let me be still.
